text:
On the threshold of the hut stands María;

the shadows of her eyes are rivals

of those shadows the coffee groves give

when day begins to fall asleep...


She is a girl who dreams and raves,

if one speaks to her of the lad with the shawls,

and she shells corn into aprons

and scents the nearness with love...


When at the river she spreads white clothes

—beside the pool where the water stands—

under the love of the hut's moon,


the white clothes pretend, from nearby

hills, to be a band of doves

pecking at stars in the river...

translation.title: White Clothes
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the white laundry becoming doves at the river.
